system_overview: This is a utility module providing basic operations on binary relations represented as Boolean-valued functions over a finite set. It defines standard relational properties (reflexivity, irreflexivity, symmetry, asymmetry, transitivity) and algorithms for computing the transitive closure, reflexive transitive closure, and connectivity of a relation. It serves as a reusable library for specifications that reason about graph structure.
actors_and_components: There are no actors or processes. The module defines pure mathematical operators on relations and sets.
state_variables: NOT_SPECIFIED. This is a definitional module with no state variables or state transitions.
initial_state: NOT_SPECIFIED. This module defines no initial state.
actions: NOT_SPECIFIED. This module defines no actions or state transitions.
safety_properties: NOT_SPECIFIED. This module defines no safety properties.
liveness_properties: NOT_SPECIFIED. This module defines no liveness properties.
model_bounds: The operators are parameterized by a relation (a Boolean function on pairs) and a set. The transitive closure computation iterates up to the cardinality of the set, which bounds its cost.
additional_assumptions: Relations are represented as functions from pairs of elements to Boolean values. The transitive closure algorithm uses iterated squaring up to the cardinality of the set, which is correct for finite sets. Evaluating transitive closure on large sets is computationally expensive.
